holds.title: A piece of the pond
holds.body:
Came up with a piece of ice on my head. It stayed there while I ate.

Bent my head to get the last bit of fish. The ice slid over my eyes.

For a moment I went back underwater without moving.
holds.reason: HOLD image and final line: observer reports ice on head and feeding; exact frame supports that conjunction, but substantial blur and color noise fail the image bar. The final line is an impression rather than a fully earned physical ending. Do not admit or treat this premise as spent.
holds.fictionBoundary: Ice and fish are visible and observer-attested. Ice sliding over the eyes and the sensation are invented. No novel biological mechanism is asserted.

holds.title: Where he went
holds.body:
He went under. I waited beside the hole.

His head came up farther away. Went after him under the ice.

When I came up, he was looking into the hole I had left. I stayed quiet until he looked round.
holds.reason: HOLD image: appealing open-water/ice geometry and observer-attested group movement, but tiny soft heads do not meet the image quality bar. The hide-and-seek sequence is fiction, not a claim about observer-documented intention. Needs a much stronger exact scene before further prose review.
holds.fictionBoundary: Two heads appear in separate ice openings; the observer describes three otters moving through ice. Tobias and an unnamed male companion are fictional assignments, not photographically sexed individuals.

media.attribution: (c) Jake McCumber, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Jake McCumber
media.sourcePlace: Cedar Lake, North Falmouth, Falmouth, MA, USA
media.sourceDescription: Group of three being quite playful together. When we first arrived one had its head out through a breathing hole in the ice, but it quickly popped down and none were seen for a few minutes.  Then all three started popping up through the thin ice and moved more or less together across much of the pond from south to north. Pausing in the constriction of the pond to wrestle around for quite a while.  They would dive, then come up and all three tumble around. Very fun!  Thanks to @nataliedt

Poked its head through little holes in the ice, caught a fish, watched some geese walk by, brought the fish up onto a rock and ate the whole thing before diving back into the water. 🦦

First pic, it’s got ice on its head. 🧊

Also, happy 18th birthday to iNaturalist!! Here’s my first observation of one of my favorite species! 🎂
